cells.tense: You are here, and your hands are busy holding the space between people.
cells.ask: Name out loud what you are already carrying for someone — and say it like you mean it, once, with them standing there.
cells.core:
You can feel what is moving between people before either one says it, and you give it room. Sitting with someone's bad news, keeping two people talking, leaving a room warmer than you found it — you do that work without making anyone pay for it. What you actually want sets which rooms you walk into and which ones you leave.

The cost line is where this stays real. You can stay in the room while the heaviness is in it and not take it home, and you can do the same quiet work when you are the tired one. Pay that, and the steadiness has somewhere to go — toward them, and toward yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what moves between people, and you do it without making them pay.
cells.verb: tending the feeling between people and keeping it steady
cells.place: in the pull toward what you actually want to be true

cells.tense: You are already at a conversation that has not happened yet, holding a room that is still empty.
cells.ask: Let one person take their day without you smoothing a thing for it — one day this week where you don't step in.
cells.core:
You are holding space for something that hasn't arrived. Somewhere ahead is the day they finally open up, or the fallout you are already softening, and you are working on it now — reaching for the right words before anyone has asked, absorbing friction before it forms. The pull toward what you want keeps giving you a reason to stay ready.

That readiness is real care, and it has run ahead of the moment. What you miss is not the point; what is missing is the contact, because two people cannot be met inside a room you are rehearsing alone. The load you can set down today was not handed to you, and putting it down does more for the connection than carrying it.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door where the feeling between people got set down.
cells.ask: Say one plain true thing to someone you trust, even if it comes out rough and you look away while it lands.
cells.core:
You can hold what moves between people, and you have stopped doing it. You stand at the edge of conversations and stay useful without arriving. The pull toward what you want still points somewhere. You have not disagreed with it; you just stopped following it in.

A room where this goes right has you in it, saying the awkward thing and not managing anyone's face while they take it. What looks like missing warmth is really missing facts — you reach for the feeling without grounding it in what is true, so it cannot hold. Getting accurate about one real thing is what fills the room you stepped out of.
cells.sheetLine: You know how to be warm in a room, and you have stopped arriving.

cells.tense: You are holding the space between people right now, and calling it something other than what you are doing.
cells.ask: Catch one small cut — the reply you swallowed, the story you decided not to finish — and say, this was chosen.
cells.core:
You already read the room before anyone speaks and you adjust — choosing the softer sentence, mentioning the thing so they are not blindsided, deciding who does not need to hear the ending. The care is the reason you trimmed it, and that trimming does real work.

What you want is where your attention went, and holding the space steady is how you kept it worth going toward. Sized right, cutting the sentence and keeping the peace are one act. You just have not signed it yet. Naming one cut as chosen is not boasting, and it is not cold — it puts a hand back on a lever that has been moving on its own.
cells.sheetLine: The cutting and the keeping are one move. You just haven't signed it.
